Title: SONAM and Partners to Boost Nurses' Mental Health in Kenya
NewsSummary: New project phase focuses on nurses' mental health to boost Kenya's health system.
NewsContent:
Johnson & Johnson Foundation has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening Kenya's health system by supporting a new phase of the Nurse & Midwife Alliance project, which will now be known as the Nurse Alliance and Mental Health Workforce Strengthening Project. 

This phase will focus on elevating the role of nurses by prioritizing their mental wellbeing, an essential pillar in building resilient and effective health systems. Practicing nurses will be selected to undergo specialized mental health training, enhancing their capacity in this critical area and, in turn, contributing to a stronger mental health and overall healthcare system in Kenya.

This commitment was formalised at an inception meeting. Mr Anthony Gitau, Director of Global Community Impact of sub-Saharan Africa and Regina Njoroge Regeru, Senior Manager for Program Delivery & Impact (EMEA) from Johnson & Johnson were present. 

"The School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa (SONAM EA) is always at the forefront of advancing nursing and midwifery education and leadership in Kenya and beyond through evidence-based research, innovative training, and capacity building," said Professor Eunice Ndirangu-Mugo, Dean, SONAM EA. "Partnerships such as these ensure that quality nursing education is accessible to all."

This second phase will bring in strategic partners to support the project's focus on improving nurses' mental health and wellbeing. It will also include expanding the training of the current mental health care workers across the country, while SONAM EA will continue to play a convening and coordinating role.

The strategic partnership also includes Kamili Mental Health Organisation, a long-time partner of Johnson & Johnson Foundation, which will assess, shortlist, and mentor the nurses selected for specialised psychiatric training. Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) will provide psychiatric nursing training, while the University of Nairobi will assess the project's impact. The Financing Alliance for Health will take the lead in establishing and managing the project secretariat.

The Nurse and Midwife Alliance (NMA) is a collaborative initiative between the Ministry of Health, the Nursing Council of Kenya, nursing associations, and AKU's School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa.
